data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's proposed distinguishing evidence—comparing the panel's variance across different checklists to the expert's variance across different framings—fails to identify a genuine reliability gain over mere compliance. If the panel blindly complies with whatever checklist it is handed, it will naturally show low variance whenever the alternate checklists are of similar quality, producing the exact same 'robustness' signature SRC_001 predicts for a genuine gain. Conversely, if all alternate checklists share a common systematic bias, the panel will faithfully comply and produce consistently wrong answers with low variance, satisfying SRC_001's criterion while having zero reliability. The evidence does not isolate a panel-specific information-processing advantage.
